items.informal_name: Existence of Monic Polynomial with Coefficients in Ideal Powers for Integral Elements
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S] {I : Ideal R} {x : S},
  IsIntegral (↥(Algebra.adjoin R {x | ∃ r ∈ I, Polynomial.C r * Polynomial.X = x})) (Polynomial.C x * Polynomial.X) →
    ∃ p, p.Monic ∧ (Polynomial.aeval x) p = 0 ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ), p.coeff i ∈ I ^ (p.natDegree - i)
items.informal_description: If $ x $ is integral over the algebra generated by the set $\{rX \mid r \in I\}$ (where $ rX $ denotes the polynomial with coefficient $ r $ in degree 1), then there exists a monic polynomial $ p \in R[X] $ such that $ p(x) = 0 $ and for every coefficient $ p_i $ of $ p $, $ p_i \in I^{\deg(p) - i} $, where $ \deg(p) $ is the degree of $ p $.

items.informal_name: Monic Polynomial Criterion for Integral Elements in Ideal Extensions
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  [Algebra.IsIntegral R S] {I : Ideal R} {x : S},
  x ∈ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) I →
    ∃ p, p.Monic ∧ (Polynomial.aeval x) p = 0 ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ), i ≠ p.natDegree → p.coeff i ∈ I
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ and $ S $ be commutative rings with $ S $ an $ R $-algebra, and let $ I $ be an ideal of $ R $. If $ x \in S $ is integral over $ R $ and lies in the extension ideal $ I \cdot S $, then there exists a monic polynomial $ p \in R[X] $ such that $ p(x) = 0 $ and all coefficients of $ p $, except the leading coefficient, belong to $ I $.

items.informal_name: Integral Element Criterion via Monic Polynomial Evaluation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {x : A}
  {p : Polynomial R}, p.Monic → p.natDegree ≠ 0 → IsIntegral R ((Polynomial.aeval x) p) → IsIntegral R x
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative ring, $ A $ an $ R $-algebra, and $ x \in A $. If $ p \in R[X] $ is a monic polynomial of positive degree such that $ p(x) $ is integral over $ R $, then $ x $ is integral over $ R $.

items.informal_name: Existence of Monic Polynomial with Coefficients in Ideal Powers for Integral Elements in Image of Ideal
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  [Algebra.IsIntegral R S] {I : Ideal R} {x : S},
  x ∈ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) I →
    ∃ p, p.Monic ∧ (Polynomial.aeval x) p = 0 ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ), p.coeff i ∈ I ^ (p.natDegree - i)
items.informal_description: Let $ R \subseteq S $ be an integral extension of commutative rings. If $ x \in S $ lies in the image of an ideal $ I \subseteq R $ under the canonical algebra homomorphism $ R \to S $, then there exists a monic polynomial $ p \in R[X] $ such that $ p(x) = 0 $ and for every coefficient $ p_i $ of $ p $, $ p_i \in I^{\deg(p) - i} $, where $ \deg(p) $ denotes the natural degree of $ p $.

items.informal_name: Integral Element Criterion via Monic Polynomial Evaluation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_4} {A : Type u_5} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {x : A}
  {p : Polynomial A},
  p.Monic →
    p.natDegree ≠ 0 → IsIntegral R (Polynomial.eval x p) → (∀ (i : ℕ), IsIntegral R (p.coeff i)) → IsIntegral R x
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ and $ A $ be commutative rings with $ A $ an $ R $-algebra. If $ p \in A[X] $ is a monic polynomial of positive degree such that each coefficient of $ p $ is integral over $ R $, and $ p(x) $ is integral over $ R $, then $ x $ is integral over $ R $.

items.informal_name: Integral Element iff Leading Coefficient Divides Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [IsDomain R] [inst_3 : Algebra R S]
  [IsIntegrallyClosed R] [IsDomain S] [Module.IsTorsionFree R S] {s : S} {p : Polynomial R},
  (Polynomial.aeval s) p = 0 →
    p ≠ 0 →
      (∀ (q : Polynomial R), q.Monic → (Polynomial.aeval s) q = 0 → p.degree ≤ q.degree) →
        (IsIntegral R s ↔ Polynomial.C p.leadingCoeff ∣ p)
items.informal_description: Let $ p $ be a non-zero polynomial in $ R[X] $ such that $ p(s) = 0 $ and $ p $ has minimal degree among all monic polynomials with $ s $ as a root. Then, $ s $ is integral over $ R $ if and only if the leading coefficient of $ p $ divides $ p $ in $ R[X] $.

items.informal_name: Minimal Polynomial of an Integral Element is Monic
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : Ring B] [inst_2 : Algebra A B] {x : B},
  IsIntegral A x → (minpoly A x).Monic
items.informal_description: For an element $ x $ integral over a ring $ A $, the minimal polynomial $ \minpoly_A(x) $ is monic, meaning its leading coefficient is 1 in $ A $.

items.informal_name: Integral Element over a Ring via a Homomorphism
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → {A : Type u_3} → [inst : CommRing R] → [inst_1 : Ring A] → (R →+* A) → A → Prop
items.informal_description: An element $ x $ in a ring $ A $ is integral over a ring $ R $ with respect to a ring homomorphism $ f : R \to A $ if there exists a monic polynomial $ p $ with coefficients in $ R $ such that evaluating $ p $ at $ x $ (with coefficients mapped through $ f $) yields zero, i.e., $ p(f(r_n), \dots, f(r_0))(x) = 0 $ where $ p = r_n X^n + \dots + r_0 $.
